overview: Speech-language pathologists help people who have trouble speaking, understanding language or swallowing. They test and assess clients, plan treatment, run therapy sessions and track progress, working with children in schools and adults after strokes or injuries. O*NET rates knowledge of English language at 4.89 out of 5 for this job, and critical thinking and active listening at 4.12. A master's degree is required, held by 89% in O*NET data, plus a state license. The BLS May 2025 median is $97,870 across 183,390 jobs. Paperwork deadlines are tight, but most work regular hours.
pay: Speech-language pathologists earn a median of $97,870, and the top 10% earn $134,160 or more. California has the highest state median at $118,970, 22% above the national figure. Texas has the most jobs, 19,120, at a median of $99,910, followed by California and New York. Health care settings often pay more than schools.

faq.q: How much do speech-language pathologists make?
faq.a: The BLS May 2025 median is $97,870 a year. The middle half earn between $77,730 and $114,570. California, Colorado ($110,750) and the District of Columbia ($109,380) pay the most, while Louisiana ($69,610) and South Dakota ($65,680) have the lowest state medians.

faq.q: What degree do you need to be a speech-language pathologist?
faq.a: You need a master's degree in speech-language pathology, which 89% hold in O*NET data, plus supervised clinical hours. Most states also require a license and many employers want the national CCC-SLP certification. There are 4 related majors, including communication sciences and disorders.

faq.q: What does a speech-language pathologist do every day?
faq.a: Most days include therapy sessions, assessments, report writing and meetings with families, teachers or doctors. O*NET rates learning strategies, writing and speaking at 4 out of 5 for this job. In O*NET data the job ranks above 98% of U.S. jobs for working with people.

faq.q: What jobs are similar to speech-language pathologist?
faq.a: The closest moves are Genetic Counselors (79% match), postsecondary health specialties teachers (79%) and nursing instructors (77%), based on O*NET 31.0. Genetic Counselors earn $100,040, 2% more, according to BLS May 2025, but need a separate master's degree.
